- `598-conditions-of-office-for-local-elected-representatives-free-mandate-fair-compensation-lawful-removal-and-no-self-government-by-attrition.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the **conditions of office of local elected representatives as a constitutional operating condition**: councillors, mayors, and other directly elected local officeholders should be able to exercise a free mandate with adequate compensation, time compatibility, facilities, training, narrow law-set incompatibilities, and strong protection against arbitrary suspension, trustee substitution, or intimidation — so local self-government is not hollowed out by unpaid exhaustion, factional starvation, or discretionary removal.
- `602-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-steward-cells-municipal-general-government-metropolitan-systems-democracy-regional-territorial-platforms-national-guarantor-states-continental-compacts-and-global-treaty-narrow-waists.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should give each scope a distinct governing vocation and a minimum complete kit: micro-local units as visible stewardship and signal cells; municipalities as the first full general-purpose governments of ordinary life; metropolitan governments as democratically legitimated operators of shared urban systems; regional, provincial, or state governments as territorial-platform governments for landscapes, hospitals, grids, universities, and shared rule; nations as guarantor states for equal citizenship, redistribution, macro-stability, and constitutional settlement; continental bodies as bounded compact governments for cross-border mobility, markets, and infrastructures; and global institutions as treaty-bound narrow waists for peace, commons, alerting, and standards rather than as a fake world domestic state.
- `610-accountability-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-scrutiny-audit-disclosure-complaints-review-and-no-government-by-jurisdictional-gap.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **accountability home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, and administrative one: its own scrutiny forum, named records-and-disclosure duties, internal control and audit proportionate to risk, external audit and integrity jurisdiction, complaint and review routes that ordinary people can actually find, and explicit accountability for operators and contractors so the territory is not really governed in the gaps between municipalities, agencies, and the state.
- `614-knowledge-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-observatories-territorial-indicators-basemaps-scenario-capacity-and-no-government-by-fragmented-spreadsheets.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **knowledge home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, and participatory one: a territorially coherent observatory, common basemaps and boundary files, a published indicator set at the scale actually being governed, lawful data-sharing and evaluation capacity, open methods and release discipline, and visible routes from evidence into plans and budgets — so the shared tier stops governing through municipal spreadsheet fragments, ministry leftovers, vendor dashboards, and dueling numbers.
- `615-service-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-service-authorities-operator-chains-commissioning-continuity-and-no-government-by-memorandum-network.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **service home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, and knowledge one: a visible split among authority, operator, and regulator; a named territorial service map showing what stays local and what becomes shared; lawful commissioning, franchising, or direct-operation routes where system services are real; service standards, continuity duties, and fallback rules that survive contracts and politics; and clear public entry and complaint handoffs — so the territory stops being governed through memoranda, host-city favors, improvised consortia, and operator clubs.
- `618-regulatory-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-licensing-permits-standards-inspection-enforcement-and-no-government-by-operator-rulebook.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **regulatory home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, planning, and capital ones: a visible territorial rulebook, named licensing and permitting lanes where risk demands them, a clear separation among rule-maker, regulator, operator, and reviewer, proportionate inspection and enforcement, and no government by operator rulebook.
- `620-workforce-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-employer-status-recruitment-training-labor-relations-and-no-government-by-borrowed-payroll.md` — Real metropolitan or regional government needs its own **employer constitution**: a named employer of record, merit-based staffing and progression, explicit pay and labor-relations rules, bounded reliance on secondment, visible workforce metrics, and a transition path out of borrowed payroll.
- `621-digital-operating-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-case-systems-identity-access-release-discipline-and-no-government-by-portal-shell.md` — Real metropolitan or regional government needs its own **digital operating constitution**: a named digital authority, canonical case/workflow and records systems, explicit identity-and-access rules, bounded interoperable exchange, release and incident discipline, continuity safeguards, and channel parity — not government by portal shell.
- `626-public-communication-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-canonical-channels-corrections-inclusive-reach-and-no-government-by-press-release-federation.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it should acquire an explicit **public-communication home**: a named official communications function distinct from party or campaign messaging; one canonical set of channels for notices, updates, warnings, and explanations; correction and version trails; multilingual and accessible publication discipline; clear docking between general information and legal notice; and archival capture of official statements so the territory does not govern through host-city press offices, operator fragments, screenshots, and rumor.
- `665-external-commitment-landing-paths-signature-ratification-transposition-direct-effect-operational-owners-and-no-treaty-by-press-release.md` — Cross-border and global commitments should not stop at signature or ratification: an honest polity should show the full **landing path** from external commitment to domestic legal effect, operational owners, budgeting, reporting, review, and subnational fit, so treaty participation does not masquerade as implementation.
- `692-shared-regime-digital-and-cyber-operating-constitutions-system-owners-identity-and-access-admin-tiers-change-windows-incident-response-vulnerability-disclosure-backups-recovery-vendor-lanes-and-no-secretariat-by-shared-password.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed digital-and-cyber operating constitution** that separates system ownership, identity and access, privileged administration, change and release control, incident response, vulnerability disclosure, vendor and cloud access, backup and restoration, recovery targets, and degraded-mode continuity — so the regime is not actually run through shared passwords, orphan systems, incident backlog, or recovery theater.
- `694-shared-regime-statistics-and-indicator-constitutions-designation-methodology-metadata-revisions-quality-assurance-release-calendars-and-no-governance-by-number-theater.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed statistics-and-indicator constitution** that separates designated official series from exploratory analytics, indicator ownership from political sponsorship, methodology from messaging, metadata from headline numbers, revisions from corrections, and release discipline from communications convenience — so evidence does not decay into number theater, indicator shopping, or policy-by-dashboard without professional standards.
- `696-shared-regime-evaluation-and-learning-constitutions-workplans-independence-management-response-recommendation-tracking-after-action-review-and-no-regime-by-report-shelf.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed evaluation-and-learning constitution** that separates workplan setting, commissioning, evaluator independence, evaluation from audit or monitoring, management response, recommendation tracking, public release, and structured learning loops such as after-action review — so institutional learning does not decay into report shelfware, recommendation theater, or “lessons learned” with no decision route.
- `703-interface-packets-for-lane-typed-government-stacks-lead-lanes-handoffs-shared-facts-escalation-clocks-and-no-governance-by-glue-folklore.md` — Once the archive has split a composite field into lane-sized scope packets, it should also publish one **interface packet** for the resulting typed stack: name the lead for each lane, the handoff triggers between lanes, the shared facts and records that must travel, the timing and escalation rules, the fiscal and liability crosswalks, and the public route map, so distributed government does not collapse back into blame circulation, duplicate work, or quiet recentralization by whoever controls the glue.
- `707-sunset-packets-for-obsolete-government-lanes-bodies-and-temporary-machinery-review-triggers-successor-homes-residue-registers-closure-proof-and-no-immortal-institutions-by-inherited-backlog.md` — Once a field has repair packets, it should also publish one **sunset packet** whenever review shows that a lane, body, or temporary governance machine no longer deserves to exist in live form — naming the trigger, the successor home or true extinction rule, the rights and service floors that still bind during wind-down, the residue register for cases, contracts, assets, staff, records, data, debt, and public-facing channels, the closure proof, and the reactivation rule — so obsolete institutions do not stay alive merely because they still have backlog, leases, websites, or logos.
- `708-evidence-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-shared-indicators-trigger-maps-blind-spot-registers-assurance-rhythm-and-no-government-by-dashboard-vibes.md` — Lane-typed government fields should publish one compact **evidence packet** that names the shared indicators, signal owners, trigger map, blind-spot register, and assurance rhythm used to judge the field — so control planes, mode shifts, repair packets, and sunset reviews run on explicit evidence with known gaps rather than on anecdotes, heroic operator memory, or dashboard theater.
- `713-delegation-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-principal-lane-reserved-powers-operator-chains-step-in-rights-and-no-public-duty-by-outsourced-wrapper.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, and amendment discipline for a field, it should also publish one narrow **delegation packet** saying which slice of the field is still constitutionally owned by the public lane, which execution work may be delegated to public bodies, contractors, concessionaires, nonprofits, co-operatives, or platforms, what powers remain non-delegable, what contract-management and records capacity the principal must retain, what step-in and handback rights keep continuity real, and what review route prevents public duty from disappearing into an outsourced wrapper.
- `715-capability-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-employer-lane-merit-floor-training-ladders-surge-rosters-and-no-government-by-borrowed-payroll.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, and a fiscal packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **capability packet** saying which lane is the employer of record and capability steward, what minimum in-house core the field must retain, what merit and qualification floor applies, what training and profession ladders sustain scarce skills, what secondment and surge rules are allowed, and what vacancy or churn triggers open repair or redesign — so the field does not rely on borrowed payroll, consultant memory, or permanent emergency staffing to remain governmental at all.
- `717-asset-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-estate-fleet-equipment-condition-discipline-handback-and-no-government-by-orphan-assets.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, and an information packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **asset packet** saying which lane owns and stewards the field’s estate, fleet, equipment, depots, labs, stores, and critical spares; who holds custody, maintenance, calibration, and replacement duty; what condition and resilience floor applies; what lease, host-site, or operator dependencies exist; and what handback rule survives exit or transfer — so the field does not decay into government by orphan assets, lease camouflage, or maintenance exile.
- `718-service-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-whole-service-front-doors-route-classes-service-floors-continuity-and-no-government-by-front-door-scatter.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, an information packet, and an asset packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **service packet** saying what outcome the field’s service actually promises, which lane owns that promise, what front doors and route classes the public may use, what clocks and service floors bind, how channels and operators compose into one whole service, and what continuity and fallback rules survive overload, outage, provider failure, or redesign — so the field does not decay into government by front-door scatter, route roulette, or service-standard theater.

## oversight

- `404-contestable-automation-and-appeals-routing.md` — No consequential automated system should be allowed to operate without a visible path from **notice** to **reason** to **override** to **appeal** to **remedy**.
- `406-federation-safe-identity-and-delegated-authority.md` — Public digital identity should prove **what role a person can act in, for whom, for how long, and under what limits** without forcing total account fusion or unnecessary identity disclosure.
- `410-public-deployment-registries-for-automated-state-action.md` — When public institutions use automated or AI-assisted systems that shape decisions, entitlements, enforcement, or public interaction, there should be a **living deployment registry** that shows what is in use, in what phase, under whose authority, and with what transparency record.
- `416-named-signoff-delegation-and-operator-training.md` — No consequential public automation should be ownerless. Every system should have a visible **sign-off chain**, a clear **delegation ladder**, and named or at least role-identified people responsible for operation, oversight, communications, and remedy.
- `417-retest-after-material-change-and-periodic-reapproval.md` — Evidence for a public automated system expires. When the system, its data, its oversight practice, or its context changes in a material way, it should be **retested and reapproved**; even without a trigger event, high-impact systems should face a periodic reapproval clock.
- `421-public-impact-assessment-dossiers-and-peer-review-before-live-use.md` — Before public automated decisions go live, operators should publish a compact **assessment dossier** that combines impact scoring, context-specific rights analysis, independent review, and accountable sign-off.
- `433-approved-use-case-registers-no-go-zones-and-tool-access-tiers.md` — Public bodies should not approve AI tools in the abstract; they should approve named use cases, publish or record no-go zones, and tie access tiers to data sensitivity, workflow role, and public impact.
- `434-override-telemetry-escalation-queues-and-second-look-sampling.md` — Human oversight is not real unless overrides, disagreements, and stop decisions are counted, reviewed, and turned into operating changes instead of disappearing as private friction.
- `439-legal-authority-maps-scope-gates-and-jurisdiction-labels.md` — A public AI system should not reach consequential use until the operating team can name the **decision it affects, the authority that permits it, the scope test that brings it under governance, and the review route that governs challenges to it**.
- `442-maker-checker-separation-independent-challenge-and-fallback-review.md` — Consequential public AI should separate **builders, operators, approvers, and reviewers** enough that no single role can quietly tune, approve, and act on the same system without an independent second look or documented compensating control.
- `449-artifact-authorship-classes-generated-content-authority-labels-and-mixed-lineage.md` — Governance artifacts for consequential public AI should declare who authored the bytes — institution, supplier, affected person, system, or mixed compiler path — so machine-generated or third-party material cannot silently inherit official authority it has not earned.
- `451-canonical-disclosure-heads-frozen-citation-tips-and-stale-copy-warnings.md` — If consequential public-AI disclosures exist in multiple versions, mirrors, excerpts, or derived summaries, the institution should publish one canonical current head, preserve citation-frozen heads for historical reference, and visibly warn when a stale or branched copy is no longer authority-bearing.
- `452-authority-allowlists-integrity-pins-and-fail-closed-external-evidence-imports.md` — Consequential public AI should treat external evidence, supplier assurances, and authoritative-source materials as governed inputs with narrow authority allowlists, integrity or version pins where needed, and fail-closed blocking when authenticity or exact identity cannot be established.
- `453-lease-addressable-temporary-authority-no-auto-resume-and-fresh-reauthorization.md` — Temporary elevated authority for support, incident response, testing, or emergency accommodation should be issued as an explicit lease-addressable instance with bounded scope, expiry, and no automatic resume after interruption, restart, or session loss.
- `457-source-backed-summaries-round-trip-checks-and-no-authority-by-recap.md` — Summaries, excerpts, dashboards, FAQs, compiled dossiers, and public-facing recaps for consequential public AI should remain explicitly source-backed, round-trip-checkable, and non-authoritative by default, so compression does not silently create a new governing record.
- `460-simulated-evidence-live-operational-proof-and-no-promotion-by-proxy.md` — Consequential public-AI governance should keep simulated, replayed, staged, shadow, and live evidence in explicitly separate lanes, and no cheaper lane should silently inherit the authority of live operational proof.
- `465-confusability-budgets-disambiguation-floors-and-alias-collision-registers.md` — Consequential public-AI archives should budget confusability across system names, case states, model families, source labels, and decision routes, and require explicit disambiguation when nearby labels could cause misrouting or mistaken authority.
- `466-umbrella-records-instance-narrowing-and-no-authority-by-family.md` — Family-level, program-level, supplier-level, or umbrella governance artifacts for consequential public AI should not be treated as authority-bearing for a specific deployment, workflow, or decision route until the archive narrows them to a named instance or explicitly states the residual gap.
- `467-native-evidence-lanes-normalized-packets-and-no-semantic-reownership.md` — Consequential public-AI archives should keep native logs, vendor exports, raw witnesses, replay references, normalized packets, and downstream summaries in distinct evidence lanes so portability does not silently rewrite source semantics, missingness, or authority.
- `481-ephemeral-working-aids-decisional-capture-thresholds-and-no-shadow-dossiers.md` — Consequential public-AI operations should clearly separate ephemeral drafts, scratchpads, convenience copies, and personal working aids from authority-bearing records, but once those aids are circulated, relied on, or add unique decisional substance, they must either be captured into the governed record or barred from carrying decision weight.
- `484-epistemic-status-tags-evidence-classes-and-no-authority-by-hedge.md` — Consequential public-AI claims, notices, summaries, incident updates, and review packets should mark each load-bearing statement as observed, measured, attested, reported, inferred, disputed, or unknown, with an explicit confidence class tied to evidence completeness, so hedged prose cannot quietly launder uncertainty into authority.
- `485-effective-state-resolution-correction-graphs-and-no-authority-by-feed-order.md` — When consequential public-AI notices, status updates, corrections, withdrawals, and superseding records accumulate over time, the institution should compute and publish one deterministic effective current state from explicit lineage links, and should treat forks or unresolved ambiguity as incidents rather than letting feed order, CMS recency, or whichever copy looks newest decide authority.
- `491-adaptive-boundaries-functional-geographies-prior-consultation-and-no-frozen-maps.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat boundaries as governed instruments rather than sacred relics: review them when functional geographies drift, consult affected communities before changing them, prefer overlap or joint authority where clean redrawing is impossible, and never let inherited lines quietly dictate today’s housing markets, watersheds, or service systems.
- `495-crisis-federalism-threshold-escalation-rule-of-law-temporariness-and-handback-clocks.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should handle crises through threshold-based escalation from the lowest competent level upward, with reserve capacity and coordination available at higher tiers, global notification and commons machinery where cross-border harms exist, and emergency powers kept lawful, necessary, proportionate, temporary, and visibly handed back once ordinary authority can govern again.
- `503-intelligence-by-scope-no-local-secret-police-judicial-authorization-minimization-and-multi-key-oversight.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should keep intelligence and surveillance narrowly scoped to genuine national-security functions under public law, forbid local secret-police formation and routine law-enforcement drift, require prior independent authorization and minimization for intrusive measures, and place the whole system under layered executive, legislative, judicial, privacy, and redress oversight so secrecy never matures into ungoverned power.
- `504-defense-by-scope-civilian-control-civil-defense-no-subnational-war-machines-and-narrow-waist-collective-security.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should place war-making and armed defense at the national level under democratic civilian control and legislative budget authority, give subnational governments civil-defense and resilience roles without autonomous war machines, keep the military distinct from routine domestic order, and rely on treaty-bound regional alliances and a narrow global collective-security layer for external peace and aggression response rather than romanticizing either total sovereignty or world-state militarism.
- `529-indigenous-peoples-and-self-government-by-scope-community-authority-municipal-consent-regional-co-governance-national-plurinational-constitutionalism-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat Indigenous peoples as peoples and governing authorities rather than as cultural stakeholders inside someone else’s map: Indigenous communities and nations should retain authority over identity, membership, internal institutions, culture, and many matters of everyday law according to their own traditions and evolving consent; municipalities should share space, services, permits, and practical coexistence through negotiated respect rather than zoning override or paternal inclusion; regional bodies should co-govern watersheds, forests, transport, health, education, and other shared systems whose real catchments outrun one settlement; nations should constitutionally recognize Indigenous peoples, lands, treaties, restitution claims, fiscal powers, and free, prior and informed consent rather than forcing all authority through a unitary citizenship mold; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in rights norms, anti-extractive scrutiny, and cross-border Indigenous solidarity rather than pretending a world body can govern each people’s internal life.
- `538-money-and-payments-by-scope-local-cash-access-municipal-acceptance-national-public-money-and-global-interoperability.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat money and payments as constitutional infrastructure: households and neighbourhood institutions can surface exclusion, fraud, outage, and cash-access failures but should not mint rival monies for ordinary public life; municipalities should guarantee practical payment usability in everyday government, including cash access and acceptance where law protects it, legible public-payment channels, and inclusive collection design; metropolitan and regional institutions should coordinate shared payment touchpoints where commuting, service markets, and public agencies cross borders; nations should own legal tender, central bank money, payment-system oversight, public-payment rails, consumer protection, anti-fraud baselines, and resilience; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in message standards, cross-border interoperability, remittance quality, and data-friction reduction rather than pretending that local service design or national monetary legitimacy can be outsourced.
- `539-banking-credit-and-financial-stability-by-scope-local-relationship-lending-regional-development-finance-national-prudential-oversight-and-global-backstops.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat banking and credit as a public-risk-bearing capability rather than a private allocation game: households, workers, firms, and local institutions can surface credit exclusion, predatory products, and place-specific capital starvation but should not be left to self-insure against systemic finance; municipalities can convene local credit intelligence, public banking interfaces, and anti-exclusion measures but should not act as miniature prudential sovereigns; regional institutions should govern development banks, housing and infrastructure finance platforms, and sectoral transition tools where production systems and catchments are wider than one city; nations should own licensing, prudential supervision, macroprudential policy, deposit insurance, resolution, lender-of-last-resort functions, and the constitutional line between utility banking and speculative risk; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in supervisory standards, cross-border resolution cooperation, correspondent-finance continuity, and anti-arbitrage floors rather than pretending world technocracy can substitute for domestic democratic control.
- `547-budgeting-treasury-and-public-accounts-credible-ceilings-legislative-authority-one-treasury-and-no-government-by-fund-fog.md` — An ideal polity should turn public money into a lawful cycle of strategy, appropriation, controlled execution, and audited account: set clear fiscal objectives and medium-term ceilings, present one comprehensive budget rather than a maze of side funds, give the legislature real time and analytic capacity to approve totals and appropriations, execute through a unified treasury, chart of accounts, commitment controls, and cash planning, publish in-year reports and year-end financial statements, disclose fiscal risks honestly, and route audit findings back into correction so the state cannot govern through supplementary fog, arrears, or off-budget improvisation.
- `552-electoral-administration-by-scope-local-voter-service-municipal-operations-regional-tabulation-national-standards-and-no-government-by-partisan-referee.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat electoral administration as a permanent, professional, and politically impartial public function: keep voter-facing service and polling logistics close enough to work, size counting and tabulation to real operational catchments, reserve core rulemaking and national certification architecture to a permanent central authority bounded by law, route disputes quickly to competent review bodies, and never let the government of the day become the referee of its own election.
- `558-public-defense-and-legal-aid-by-scope-local-entry-municipal-navigation-regional-provider-capacity-national-independence-and-no-justice-by-unaffordable-counsel.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **public defense and legal aid** as a **core constitutional capacity for equal justice** rather than as charity or courthouse aftercare: keep first contact, rights information, and navigable entry close to daily life; use metropolitan, county, provincial, state, or other regional institutions for most ordinary defender offices, provider networks, and specialist capacity; reserve national government for the right itself, independent legal-aid authority design, fair funding, quality floors, and territorial equalization; and never allow **freedom, family life, housing, status, or civil survival to depend on whether a person can privately purchase counsel on short notice**.
- `560-official-statistics-and-census-institutions-by-scope-local-administrative-data-discipline-regional-capacity-national-independence-and-no-government-by-partisan-numbers.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **official statistics and census institutions** as a **constitutional public-facts system**: keep administrative-data quality, respondent support, and local enumeration logistics close to where people and records actually are; use provincial, state, regional, or other intermediate statistical institutions where territorial scale or federal structure justifies durable subject-matter capacity; reserve national government for the legal guarantees of professional independence, statistical confidentiality, census authority, coordination of the national statistical system, common methods and classifications, and public release calendars; and never allow the government of the day to decide the country’s facts by press office, police apparatus, or ministry convenience.
- `563-public-procurement-institutions-and-review-by-scope-local-needs-regional-shared-buying-national-rules-independent-challenges-and-no-government-by-emergency-sole-source-fog.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat public procurement as a governed public institution rather than a clerical back office: keep need definition, user-facing specification, and day-to-day contract management close to the service; use metropolitan, county, provincial, state, or other regional shared-buying bodies where market structure, scarce expertise, or repeated categories make pooling sensible; reserve national government for the procurement code, standard documents, core e-procurement rails, integrity controls, supplier-access baselines, independent complaint review design, and open-contracting discipline; keep the global layer narrow in interoperable standards, anti-rigging and anti-corruption cooperation, and fair cross-border conditions of competition; and never let emergency exemptions, framework sprawl, or vendor dependence turn public spending into shadow executive power.
- `564-anti-corruption-bodies-and-integrity-commissions-by-scope-local-routing-regional-case-development-national-specialization-and-no-government-by-heroic-commission.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not rely on one heroic anti-corruption commission: keep local complaint intake, disclosure routing, whistleblower handoff, and ordinary integrity advice close enough to be usable; place regional or state-level investigative and inspection capacity where corruption markets, procurement webs, and patronage chains cross municipalities or where tiny jurisdictions are too captured to investigate themselves; reserve national government for the preventive architecture required by law, high-level and cross-regional corruption, asset-declaration verification, beneficial-ownership tracing, international cooperation, and strategy coordination; keep the global layer narrow in standards, peer review, and transnational case support; and never let anti-corruption institutions become either decorative ethics theater or unreviewable prosecutor-states.
- `565-ideal-constitutional-kits-by-scope-neighborhood-voice-municipal-councils-metropolitan-democracy-regional-federal-capacity-national-solidarity-continental-compacts-and-global-narrow-waists.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat each scope as needing a **complete but scale-matched constitutional kit** — decision forum, executive administration, finance, oversight, and participation — with neighborhood institutions optimized for voice and upkeep, municipalities for general-purpose place governance, metropolitan bodies for shared urban systems, regions for major territorial platforms and shared rule, nations for rights and solidarity, continental bodies for bounded cooperation, and global institutions for mandate-bound coordination of peace, commons, alerting, and common standards.
- `569-addresses-place-names-and-administrative-geography-by-scope-community-legibility-municipal-address-authority-regional-coherence-national-reference-frames-and-no-government-by-phantom-location.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat addresses, place names, and administrative geography as constitutional infrastructure rather than clerical leftovers: communities should help surface real local names and hard-to-map places, municipalities or counties should usually be the ordinary authority for street naming and address maintenance, metropolitan or regional layers should keep cross-boundary location systems coherent where daily life and service networks spill across borders, national institutions should own the authoritative reference frame for identifiers, geocoding, administrative units, and interoperability, and continental or global bodies should provide standards rather than pretending there can be one sovereign address book for the world.
- `570-legal-entity-business-and-beneficial-ownership-registries-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-entry-desks-regional-coordination-national-public-truth-and-no-government-by-paper-shell.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat organizational identity as constitutional infrastructure rather than clerical residue: communities can help witness real economic and associational life, municipalities or counties should usually provide the reachable entry desk for ordinary business-facing registrations and permits, regional or state layers should coordinate where federal structure or market geography requires it, national or constitutional-state law should own the authoritative registry of legal persons and the rules for unique identifiers, lifecycle events, disclosure, and strike-off, beneficial ownership should be held through a public authority or tightly governed equivalent with rapid lawful access and strong update discipline, and continental or global bodies should provide interoperability rails rather than pretending there can be one sovereign company register for the world.
- `572-standards-metrology-testing-accreditation-and-conformity-assessment-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-inspection-regional-labs-national-quality-infrastructure-and-no-government-by-unverified-measurement.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **standards, metrology, testing, accreditation, and conformity assessment** as a **constitutional measurement layer**: keep user witnessing, complaint, and local inspection close to communities and municipalities; pool expensive laboratories, calibration, and specialist technical capacity at regional scale where fragmentation would waste money or degrade competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the quality-infrastructure core — measurement units, national metrology, accreditation, legal metrology, standard-setting mandates, and recognition rules — and use continental and global layers for equivalence, interoperability, and trade discipline rather than for a fantasy of one world product ministry.
- `573-administrative-procedure-permits-and-licenses-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-front-doors-regional-technical-review-national-procedure-codes-and-no-government-by-permit-maze.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **administrative procedure, permits, and licenses** as the **constitutional authorization layer** of government: keep lived fact-finding, pre-application help, and ordinary place-based intake close to communities and municipalities; pool specialist review and cross-boundary technical assessment regionally where risks or spillovers justify it; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the core procedural guarantees, common clocks, appeal architecture, and recognition rules that make the whole system legible; and use continental and global layers for interoperability, evidence exchange, and mutual recognition rather than for a fantasy of one world permit desk.
- `574-electronic-identification-signatures-seals-and-document-authentication-by-scope-community-attestation-municipal-enrollment-regional-federation-national-trust-frameworks-and-no-government-by-unverifiable-file.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **electronic identification, trust services, signatures, seals, time-stamps, and document authentication** as the **constitutional trust layer** of government: keep assisted enrollment, local fact correction, and ordinary witnessing close to people and firms; allow municipal and other frontline offices to serve as practical entry points into proofing and service use; pool federation and shared technical operations where subnational scale genuinely adds capacity; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the legal trust framework, assurance levels, authoritative source linkage, trusted lists, revocation discipline, and long-term verifiability of state acts; and use continental and global layers for standards, narrow recognition, and document authentication across borders rather than for a fantasy of one world identity stack.
- `575-official-notice-service-and-proof-of-delivery-by-scope-community-contact-municipal-address-for-service-regional-coordination-national-effect-rules-and-no-government-by-presumed-receipt.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **official notice, service of documents, proof of delivery, and legally significant receipt** as the **constitutional contact layer** of government: keep contact correction, local explanation, and assisted receipt close to people and firms; use municipalities and other frontline offices as ordinary points for address-for-service maintenance and help; pool specialist field service and hard-to-reach delivery work where subnational scale adds competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the rules that determine when notice counts, when clocks start, what proof suffices, and how failed delivery affects legal effect; and use continental and global layers for narrow treaty-bound cross-border service rather than for a fantasy of one world notification stack.
- `576-base-registries-identifiers-reference-data-and-interoperability-by-scope-community-error-surfacing-municipal-data-stewardship-regional-brokers-national-authoritative-sources-and-no-government-by-contradictory-copies.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **base registries, identifiers, reference data, and interoperability** as the **constitutional integration layer** of government: keep error surfacing, assisted correction, and local fact challenge close to people and firms; use municipalities and other frontline bodies as disciplined stewards and consumers of authoritative data rather than rival sovereign databases; pool interconnection, exchange infrastructure, and semantic support above fragmented local jurisdictions where scale adds competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for designating authoritative sources, assigning identifier rules, governing access, and maintaining shared code lists and metadata; and keep continental or global roles narrow enough to support cross-border evidence exchange, schemas, and semantic alignment without becoming a world master database.
- `577-public-service-delivery-one-stop-shops-and-assisted-digital-access-by-scope-community-navigation-municipal-front-counters-regional-shared-service-centers-national-service-standards-and-no-government-by-channel-maze.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **public service delivery** as the **constitutional execution layer** of government: keep trusted navigation, assisted digital help, and ordinary human contact close to communities and municipalities; pool shared service centers, call centers, translation, queue balancing, and specialist case support above fragmented local jurisdictions where scale adds competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for service standards, life-event integration, channel parity, common status semantics, and the core rails that let services feel like one government rather than a pile of agencies; and keep continental or global roles narrow enough to support cross-border information, procedures, assistance, and evidence exchange without becoming a world ministry of customer service.
- `578-open-data-and-public-information-reuse-by-scope-community-scrutiny-municipal-publishing-regional-aggregation-national-standards-and-no-government-by-pdf-fog.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **open data and public-information reuse** as the **constitutional public-reuse layer** of government: keep community scrutiny, correction demand, and context close to the people and places described by the data; require municipalities and frontline bodies to publish routine local information in genuinely reusable ways rather than as decorative PDF dumps; pool regional aggregation, comparison, and cross-boundary publication where fragmented local release would make the public blind to shared systems; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the legal framework on reuse, licensing, metadata, machine-readable publication, privacy and confidentiality boundaries, high-value dataset rules, and catalog standards; and keep continental or global roles narrow enough to support interoperable metadata, cross-border discovery, and common high-value publication patterns without becoming one world data ministry.
- `579-scope-allocation-by-level-intimacy-spillovers-coercion-solidarity-infrastructure-commons-and-no-government-by-level-confusion.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should allocate functions by a compact **scope-allocation grammar** rather than by inherited prestige or map inertia: keep voice, stewardship, and context-heavy discretion as close to people as possible; shift authority upward when spillovers outrun local borders, when network infrastructures require shared operation, when equal-rights floors and due-process guarantees require stronger uniformity, when risk-pooling and redistribution need a wider base, and when cross-border commons or security problems cannot be solved domestically; and treat continental and global layers as **narrow-waist coordination regimes** for shared problems rather than as imitation nation-states.
- `584-common-floors-local-headroom-explicit-preemption-rules-and-no-silent-override-by-upper-tier-convenience.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **preemption and override as explicit constitutional instruments rather than as ambient higher-tier privilege**: upper levels may set rights floors, solidarity guarantees, interoperability rules, and protections against genuine cross-border harms, but they should leave subnational governments real room to go further or adapt locally unless a law clearly names the conflict, states the protected interest, consults affected governments, provides transition and finance where duties are displaced, and subjects any ceiling preemption or field occupation to review rather than letting uniformity spread by habit.
- `586-function-transfer-packs-staff-assets-records-contracts-liabilities-and-no-reassignment-by-legal-text-alone.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **any transfer of a public function across levels of government as a full transfer pack rather than a sentence in a law**: whenever a competence moves, the same settlement should also name the effective date, service standard, staff lane, asset and lease inventory, contract and procurement treatment, records and data custody, ongoing-case handoff, fiscal lane, liability rule, transition authority, dispute route, and review clock, so that decentralisation or recentralisation cannot occur by moving the headline power while leaving the receiving government to inherit an empty shell.
- `594-local-authority-associations-consortia-transfrontier-co-operation-and-no-self-government-in-isolation.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the right of local authorities to co-operate, form delivery consortia, join representative associations, and work with counterparts across borders as part of self-government itself, so municipalities and regions can pool capacity, defend common interests, and solve cross-boundary problems without being reduced to isolated administrative fragments.
- `607-democratic-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-indirect-councils-double-legitimacy-direct-election-and-no-metropolitan-rule-by-proxy.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, the honest constitutional question is not whether it needs democracy but **which democratic home fits the power**: keep indirect representation for narrow and bounded co-ordination, use double-legitimacy designs where both people and component governments must visibly count, and prefer directly elected territorial government once the body can bind residents through compulsory finance, major debt, cross-sector territorial bargaining, or durable system-shaping authority.
- `615-service-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-service-authorities-operator-chains-commissioning-continuity-and-no-government-by-memorandum-network.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **service home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, and knowledge one: a visible split among authority, operator, and regulator; a named territorial service map showing what stays local and what becomes shared; lawful commissioning, franchising, or direct-operation routes where system services are real; service standards, continuity duties, and fallback rules that survive contracts and politics; and clear public entry and complaint handoffs — so the territory stops being governed through memoranda, host-city favors, improvised consortia, and operator clubs.
- `616-planning-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-territorial-plans-plan-hierarchies-conformity-and-no-government-by-vision-deck.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **planning home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, and service ones: a territorial planning authority with a real public plan, a declared hierarchy with municipal and state plans, visible conformity or compatibility rules, infrastructure-and-land-use coupling, amendment and review clocks, and no territorial government by advisory strategy deck.
- `621-digital-operating-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-case-systems-identity-access-release-discipline-and-no-government-by-portal-shell.md` — Real metropolitan or regional government needs its own **digital operating constitution**: a named digital authority, canonical case/workflow and records systems, explicit identity-and-access rules, bounded interoperable exchange, release and incident discipline, continuity safeguards, and channel parity — not government by portal shell.
- `622-emergency-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-emergency-operations-continuity-mutual-aid-recovery-and-no-government-by-crisis-summit.md` — Real metropolitan or regional government needs its own **emergency constitution**: a named territorial emergency authority, an all-hazards risk picture, predefined escalation and mutual-aid rules, continuity of government and essential services, exercised communication and warning routes, recovery and handback discipline, and bounded extraordinary powers — not government by crisis summit.
- `630-rescoping-authority-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-administration-by-law-constitutional-bargains-by-consent-and-no-jurisdictional-rewire-by-executive-deal.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat **moving a function between scopes as a graded constitutional act**: ordinary implementation detail may be adjusted through ordinary law inside fixed competences, sectoral reallocations among existing tiers should travel through public legislation with consultation and impact proof, any move that alters the protected bargain of local or regional self-government should require the higher law and consent route appropriate to that bargain, and no executive compact, grant condition, crisis summit, or managerial workaround should be allowed to rewire who really governs what.
- `633-canonical-scope-registers-responsibility-matrices-exception-ledgers-and-no-government-by-jurisdiction-folklore.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should keep one **canonical public scope register** that shows, for each major function and lane of authority, the default legal home, territorial footprint, finance path, real delivery chain, exceptions, temporary deviations, review route, and next review date, so the stack is governed as an inspectable object rather than inferred from scattered statutes, grants, habits, and insider folklore.
- `637-scope-overrides-explicit-departure-statements-review-clocks-and-no-constitutional-clearance-by-quiet-disregard.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should allow departure from a negative or conditional **scope opinion** only through one explicit public **scope-override statement** naming the disagreement, legal authority, reasons, rejected alternatives, temporary or permanent status, review and challenge clocks, and required register updates, so the review lane is neither a hidden veto nor a decorative memo and the stack cannot be changed by quiet disregard.
- `638-clear-statement-rules-for-scope-change-interpretive-backstops-and-no-rescoping-by-ambiguity.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should adopt one public **clear-statement rule for scope change**: ambiguous statutes, grants, budgets, guidance, compacts, or software defaults should not be interpreted as materially reallocating protected competences, narrowing local or regional discretion, or creating durable new stack relations unless the instrument says so explicitly and travels with the linked scope packet, opinion, and override path where required.
- `639-scope-conformance-before-go-live-implementation-attestations-readiness-gates-and-no-stack-change-by-deployment-drift.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require one public **scope-conformance attestation before go-live** for any materially stack-altering measure: budgets, regulations, grants, contracts, staffing, digital workflows, supervisory routines, public communications, and remedy routes should be checked against the adopted packet, opinion, override, and live register so that implementation cannot quietly move power farther than law and consent actually authorised.
- `642-scope-retirement-certificates-repeal-cleanup-successor-crosswalks-and-no-constitutional-ghosting.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require one public **scope-retirement certificate** whenever a materially stack-bearing competence, exception, body, supervisory lane, or temporary upper-tier hold is repealed, handed back, merged away, or superseded: retirement should close legal authority, budgets, systems, public channels, and review routes together, preserve historical memory, and refuse any afterlife of government by leftover residue.
- `643-scope-reactivation-certificates-dormancy-fresh-clearance-and-no-constitutional-necromancy.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require one public **scope-reactivation certificate** before any materially stack-bearing authority, exception lane, shared body, or supervisory hold returns from retirement, dormancy, suspension, or expiry: old text, old systems, old habits, and old crisis muscle memory should not make public power live again without fresh legality, current rights checks, updated scope classification, and a visible register change.
- `647-scope-remand-discipline-cure-instructions-bounded-reopening-and-no-stack-redesign-by-reconsideration.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat **remand** in materially stack-altering disputes as a **bounded cure lane**, not as an open invitation to redesign the scope stack: a reviewing body that sends a package back for correction should specify exactly what defect must be cured, what remains frozen or intact, what consultation or consent must be rerun, and when the matter has crossed the line into a fresh packet, opinion, override, or constituent decision.
- `648-scope-functional-equivalence-rules-anti-circumvention-tests-and-no-stack-change-by-relabeling.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should classify **materially stack-altering moves by their real effect rather than by their chosen label**: if a grant condition, procurement framework, software default, model contract, coordination protocol, “pilot”, guidance note, or emergency instruction functionally reallocates who decides, who must comply, who pays, who may object, or which tier now governs in practice, it should travel through the same packet, opinion, override, register, and review lanes as any openly named scope change.
- `650-scope-estoppel-limits-reliance-sunk-cost-benefit-retention-and-no-stack-change-by-dependence.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should refuse to let **reliance, sunk cost, operational dependence, accepted benefits, or delayed objection manufacture constitutional title**: when a materially stack-altering move lacked the right authority, the right consent, or the right public lane, the answer should be cure, remand, override, rollback, or fresh authorization — not estoppel by familiarity, expense, or service dependency.
- `651-scope-prescription-limits-delay-bars-adverse-possession-and-no-stack-change-by-time-alone.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should not let **mere duration, delayed challenge, or long unlawful exercise** manufacture constitutional title: materially stack-altering arrangements may need continuity management, evidentiary caution, or prospective settlement after long operation, but they should not acquire lawful authority simply because they lasted, were hard to unwind, or went unchallenged for too long.
- `652-scope-desuetude-limits-abandonment-fictions-and-no-stack-change-by-atrophy.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should not let **non-use, weak use, under-enforcement, dormancy, or degraded capacity** silently extinguish protected competence: materially stack-bearing authority may require review, repair, reactivation, or even lawful reassignment, but it should not be treated as lost merely because it was not exercised often, boldly, or recently enough.
- `653-scope-source-hierarchies-authority-ladders-and-no-stack-change-by-the-loudest-surface.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should settle disputes about **who governs what** against a declared **source hierarchy** rather than against whichever surface is loudest, newest, easiest to find, or already wired into daily operations: constitutional and statutory text, authoritative judgments, and explicit scope acts should outrank derivative registers, and derivative registers should outrank budgets, contracts, software behavior, dashboards, FAQs, and public-relations residue.
- `655-scope-retroactivity-limits-future-only-defaults-curative-acts-and-no-stack-change-by-backdating.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat **materially stack-altering acts as future-facing by default**: if a sponsor wants retroactive effect, retroactive validation, or a backdated effective date, it should have to travel through an unusually narrow, explicit, legally justified lane with preserved **review routes**, **judicial remedy**, and clear **legal authority** rather than letting the stack change by historical rewrite.
- `659-scope-evidentiary-break-presumptions-burden-allocation-and-no-stack-change-by-missing-file.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat any **unrepaired evidentiary break inside a materially stack-altering reform** as a burden-allocation event rather than a neutral accident — keeping the burden on the authority that claims the scope change, continuity, legality, or harmlessness, and refusing to let missing files, broken migration, or lost metadata manufacture constitutional title by opacity.
- `666-compliance-ladders-for-shared-regimes-reporting-peer-review-inspection-dispute-settlement-remediation-suspension-and-no-treaty-by-voluntary-vibes.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **graduated compliance ladder** matched to the problem class — from reporting and peer review through technical verification, corrective action, dispute settlement, and where necessary suspension or other consequence — so co-operation does not depend on vibes and enforcement does not jump straight from silence to punishment.
- `671-shared-regime-representation-ladders-credentials-chief-delegates-alternates-observers-speaking-rights-committee-access-and-no-state-voice-by-self-appointment.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed representation ladder** that separates party or member status from delegate credentials, chief delegates from alternates and advisers, participants from observers, and speaking rights from voting rights — with accrediting authority, challenge lane, substitution rules, public roster, and functional-independence protections — so no one can conjure state or member voice by badge, donor access, press credential, or self-appointment.
- `672-shared-regime-decision-rules-agenda-gates-quorum-consensus-simple-majority-qualified-majority-double-majority-veto-limits-and-no-governance-by-fake-unanimity.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed decision constitution** that separates agenda adoption, proposal circulation, quorum to open, quorum to decide, consensus practice, simple-majority procedure, qualified-majority substantive voting, double-majority shared-rule decisions, unanimity or veto for only narrow sovereignty-sensitive questions, and deadlock breakers — so bodies can act without either fake-unanimity theater or casual majoritarian override.
- `674-shared-regime-records-and-publicity-public-private-sessions-document-registers-meeting-records-vote-records-authentic-texts-corrections-and-no-governance-by-missing-papertrail.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed documentary constitution** that separates session publicity, agenda and paper circulation, official document registers, meeting-record formats, vote records, authentic texts, correction notices, and retention or access rules — so public authority does not vanish into missing minutes, unofficial drafts, or document folklore.
- `677-shared-regime-external-participation-constitutions-accreditation-observer-categories-submissions-hearings-transparency-registers-and-no-public-power-by-lanyard.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed external-participation constitution** that separates membership from observer or accredited-participant status, standing accreditation from session registration, document access from floor rights, written submissions from negotiation rights, and consultation from decision power — so public authority does not drift toward whoever got a badge, a side-room invitation, or a privileged mailing list.
- `687-shared-regime-privileges-and-immunities-constitutions-functional-independence-jurisdiction-tax-customs-inviolability-waiver-and-no-sovereignty-cosplay.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed privileges-and-immunities authority map** that separates juridical personality, inviolability, immunity from legal process, archives and communications protection, fiscal and customs facilities, visa and entry support, category-specific treatment for representatives and officials, waiver authority, and abuse-control lanes — so institutional independence is protected without decaying into sovereignty cosplay, perk inflation, or unreviewable impunity.
- `688-shared-regime-private-law-claims-constitutions-contracts-torts-procurement-disputes-standing-claims-bodies-arbitration-insurance-and-no-immunity-without-remedy.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed review-and-remedy constitution** for private-law disputes that separates contract claims, procurement complaints, property and personal-injury claims, insurance recovery, amicable settlement, standing claims bodies where needed, arbitration clauses, waiver decisions, and payment authority — so the regime can preserve functional immunity from ordinary local courts without sliding into immunity without remedy.
- `691-shared-regime-information-classification-and-disclosure-constitutions-public-on-request-internal-confidential-strict-harm-tests-downgrading-external-sharing-and-no-secrecy-by-folder-folklore.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed information-classification-and-disclosure constitution** that separates public, request-only, internal working, confidential, strictly confidential, personal-data, and security-sensitive lanes — with named marking authority, handling rules, external-sharing conditions, review clocks, and request-and-review paths — so information is governed by visible rules instead of folder folklore, indiscriminate secrecy, or accidental disclosure by habit.
- `711-oversight-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-audit-inspection-ombuds-parliamentary-scrutiny-follow-up-ledgers-and-no-self-certification-by-the-same-office.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, an evidence packet, a challenge packet, and a participation packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **oversight packet** naming which independent bodies outside the live control plane may inspect which questions, on what triggers and calendars, with what access powers, response duties, and follow-up ledger, so the field is not left certifying itself by the same office that designed, funded, or operated it.
- `712-amendment-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-change-classes-ratification-ladders-version-ledgers-drift-logs-and-no-field-redesign-by-memo.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, an evidence packet, challenge and participation packets, and an oversight packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **amendment packet** naming which changes are merely tuning and which are constitutional, who may propose them, what participation and scrutiny gates apply, what ratification ladder adopts them, when they take effect, and what version ledger plus drift log keeps the field from being redesigned by memo, queue custom, temporary exception, or software default.
- `713-delegation-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-principal-lane-reserved-powers-operator-chains-step-in-rights-and-no-public-duty-by-outsourced-wrapper.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, and amendment discipline for a field, it should also publish one narrow **delegation packet** saying which slice of the field is still constitutionally owned by the public lane, which execution work may be delegated to public bodies, contractors, concessionaires, nonprofits, co-operatives, or platforms, what powers remain non-delegable, what contract-management and records capacity the principal must retain, what step-in and handback rights keep continuity real, and what review route prevents public duty from disappearing into an outsourced wrapper.
- `714-fiscal-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-operating-base-equalization-spine-reserves-capital-lanes-and-no-government-by-grant-fog.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, and delegation rules for a field, it should also publish one narrow **fiscal packet** saying what recurring operating base actually funds the field, which lane holds budget and treasury authority, what equalization or solidarity rule corrects uneven burdens, what reserve and contingency ladder keeps shocks from becoming constitutional panic, what capital and debt lane is lawful, and what grants may supplement but not substitute for an honest money constitution.
- `715-capability-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-employer-lane-merit-floor-training-ladders-surge-rosters-and-no-government-by-borrowed-payroll.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, and a fiscal packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **capability packet** saying which lane is the employer of record and capability steward, what minimum in-house core the field must retain, what merit and qualification floor applies, what training and profession ladders sustain scarce skills, what secondment and surge rules are allowed, and what vacancy or churn triggers open repair or redesign — so the field does not rely on borrowed payroll, consultant memory, or permanent emergency staffing to remain governmental at all.
- `716-information-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-canonical-case-home-access-model-sharing-boundaries-retention-clocks-and-no-government-by-portal-shell.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, and a capability packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **information packet** saying where the field’s canonical case and record homes live, which surface is the system of record and which are only presentation or intake layers, what role-and-access model governs staff and delegates, what sharing boundaries and information agreements apply, what retention/export/handback rules preserve public memory, and what recovery path keeps the field governable when platforms, vendors, or host systems fail — so the field does not become government by portal shell, spreadsheet relay, or vendor-admin shadow.
- `717-asset-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-estate-fleet-equipment-condition-discipline-handback-and-no-government-by-orphan-assets.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, and an information packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **asset packet** saying which lane owns and stewards the field’s estate, fleet, equipment, depots, labs, stores, and critical spares; who holds custody, maintenance, calibration, and replacement duty; what condition and resilience floor applies; what lease, host-site, or operator dependencies exist; and what handback rule survives exit or transfer — so the field does not decay into government by orphan assets, lease camouflage, or maintenance exile.
- `718-service-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-whole-service-front-doors-route-classes-service-floors-continuity-and-no-government-by-front-door-scatter.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, an information packet, and an asset packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **service packet** saying what outcome the field’s service actually promises, which lane owns that promise, what front doors and route classes the public may use, what clocks and service floors bind, how channels and operators compose into one whole service, and what continuity and fallback rules survive overload, outage, provider failure, or redesign — so the field does not decay into government by front-door scatter, route roulette, or service-standard theater.

## participation

- `405-civic-participation-ops-and-decision-legibility.md` — Participation should be run as an **operational system with visible commitments**, not as a symbolic consultation layer detached from decisions.
- `418-bounded-beta-and-parallel-run-gates-before-consequential-use.md` — Public automated systems should not jump from lab confidence to civic dependence. Before a system becomes consequential in live operations, it should pass through a **bounded beta or parallel-run gate** with explicit scope limits, learning goals, fallback arrangements, and a named decision about whether it is actually ready for live reliance.
- `490-representation-by-scope-neighborhood-voice-metro-election-federal-shared-rule-and-deliberative-complement.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not clone one representation formula at every scale: it should use close, participatory voice where place knowledge is richest, directly elected councils for city and metro systems, population-based representation for common citizenship, territorial shared-rule chambers where constituent units need a federal voice, and representative deliberative mini-publics as a complement for hard cross-cutting questions.
- `491-adaptive-boundaries-functional-geographies-prior-consultation-and-no-frozen-maps.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat boundaries as governed instruments rather than sacred relics: review them when functional geographies drift, consult affected communities before changing them, prefer overlap or joint authority where clean redrawing is impossible, and never let inherited lines quietly dictate today’s housing markets, watersheds, or service systems.
- `492-competence-conflict-routing-intergovernmental-arbitration-and-no-settlement-by-fiscal-blackmail.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should route intergovernmental disputes through declared consultation, mediation, and final legal-arbitral decision rather than through improvisation, prestige contests, or fund-withholding coercion, so conflicts over powers, duties, and money are settled by rules that preserve both common government and lower-tier self-rule.
- `498-constitutional-change-by-scope-local-charters-double-majorities-constituent-consent-and-no-silent-recentralization.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should be adaptable without being easy to hijack: routine institutional adjustment should happen through ordinary law or local charters where appropriate, but changes to the territorial bargain, rights architecture, or division of powers should require heightened procedures, constituent-unit consent where federal balance is affected, and fair consultation or referendum only on constitutionally grounded terms, with no unilateral recentralization by ordinary statute, fiscal leverage, or emergency drift.
- `500-political-competition-by-scope-civic-lists-durable-parties-public-finance-spending-discipline-and-no-incumbency-self-dealing.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should make political competition open enough for renewal and structured enough for governability: local elections should allow civic lists, independents, and low-friction entry where that fits; larger scales need durable parties that aggregate interests across territory and time; and public finance, spending discipline, timely disclosure, equal treatment, and anti-incumbency rules should keep wealth and state machinery from becoming the real ballot language.
- `501-public-sphere-by-scope-community-media-public-service-independence-ownership-transparency-and-civic-information-commons.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat a plural information order as constitutional infrastructure: community and local media should have legal room and sustainable support, public service media should be editorially independent and publicly accountable rather than government-controlled, media ownership and state support should be transparent, and digital distribution rules should protect access to diverse public-interest information instead of quietly collapsing the public sphere into either oligarchy or platform dependence.
- `502-public-safety-by-scope-prevention-first-local-legitimacy-metro-serious-crime-coordination-and-rights-locked-cooperation.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat public safety as a scale-matched civic function rather than a single armed hierarchy: neighborhoods and municipalities should lead on prevention, trust, and visible order; metropolitan and regional bodies should coordinate spillover systems and serious-crime patterns; nations should set rights, training, and investigative baselines; and international police cooperation should stay narrow, ordinary-law, human-rights-bound, and never become a back door for political policing.
- `509-work-and-income-security-by-scope-local-access-regional-labour-markets-national-social-insurance-and-transnational-portability.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should split work governance by function and scale: neighborhoods and municipalities remove practical barriers to participation and surface abuse; metropolitan and regional institutions govern the real labour market through mobility, matching, skills, and transition platforms; nations set labour law, collective-bargaining architecture, minimum standards, and social insurance; regional compacts widen portability and fair mobility where states consent; and global institutions anchor labour rights and migrant-worker protections without pretending to run every labour market from Geneva.
- `516-markets-and-company-power-by-scope-local-entry-metro-space-national-antitrust-and-fair-global-rules.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern markets by keeping entry barriers, permits, public procurement access, and everyday consumer signal detection close to local life; using metropolitan and regional institutions to manage commercial geography, logistics, and market systems that cross municipal borders; reserving competition law, merger control, company law, securities rules, labour and consumer floors, and strategic industrial discipline to the nation; and using the global layer for trade predictability, anti-cartel cooperation, tax-base protection, and narrow common rules that prevent regulatory arbitrage without constitutionalizing corporate power above democracy.
- `519-innovation-and-industrial-policy-by-scope-local-entrepreneurship-regional-clusters-national-missions-and-open-global-coordination.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern innovation and industrial policy by keeping entrepreneurship support, practical diffusion, local supplier development, and maker or skills ecosystems close to firms and workers; using metropolitan and regional institutions to cultivate clusters, applied research linkages, transition strategies, and shared innovation infrastructure; reserving mission setting, major R&D finance, competition-safe sector policy, strategic trade and resilience choices, and national innovation floors to the nation; and keeping the global layer narrow, focused on open science, standards, subsidy transparency, technology cooperation, and anti-arbitrage trade rules rather than a world ministry of industry.
- `520-care-and-support-by-scope-household-reciprocity-municipal-services-regional-care-systems-national-social-insurance-and-global-worker-protection.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat care as civic infrastructure rather than private fallout: households, kin, and neighbors can contribute reciprocity but should not be the welfare state; municipalities should make childcare, disability support, elder support, and respite actually reachable; regional bodies should coordinate workforce pipelines, specialist and long-term-care systems, and discharge pathways that cross municipal lines; nations should guarantee paid leave, cash and service entitlements, labour standards, and financing pools; and the global layer should stay narrow but real in labour standards, migrant-care-worker protection, and knowledge exchange rather than pretending families can absorb demographic change forever.
- `524-children-and-youth-by-scope-local-belonging-municipal-voice-regional-opportunity-national-guarantees-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern childhood and youth as a full citizenship-building architecture rather than a sentimental side issue: families, peers, schools, and neighborhood institutions should make belonging and safety real; municipalities should build child-friendly streets, services, and participation channels; regional bodies should coordinate transport, child protection pathways, specialist services, and opportunity systems that outrun one town; nations should guarantee rights, income floors, education and care baselines, and fair transitions to adulthood; and the global layer should protect child-rights norms, anti-exploitation baselines, and cross-border solidarity without becoming a world parent.
